description.summary: per-window rendering scale, opacity, corners and shadow

protocol.description:
This fork-only protocol (newm-river, a fork of river) lets the river-window-management-v1 window manager draw a window scaled and translucent without resizing it: a camera zoom, not a resize. The window keeps its dimensions, its configures and its input region; only the way river draws it changes.
Scale and opacity are rendering state as defined by river_window_manager_v1: they may only be modified during a manage or render sequence and are applied with the next render_finish request.
Version 2 adds rounded corners and a shadow (also rendering state), and snapshots: a copy of a window's last frame that the window manager can scale, move and fade after the window closed (a close animation).
The key words "must", "must not", "required", "shall", "shall not", "should", "should not", "recommended", "may", and "optional" in this document are to be interpreted as described in IETF RFC 2119.

interface.name: newm_river_render_v1
interface.description: This global interface should only be advertised to the client if the river_window_manager_v1 global is also advertised. Only the active window manager owns river_window_v1 objects, so only it can use this interface.

entry.name: object_already_created
entry.summary: a newm_river_window_render_v1 already exists for the window

request.name: destroy
request.description: This request indicates that the client will no longer use the newm_river_render_v1 object. Objects created from it are not affected.

request.name: get_window_render

description.summary: get the rendering object of a window

request.description:
Create a newm_river_window_render_v1 for the given window. It is a protocol error to make this request more than once for a window while the previous object exists.
If the river_window_v1 is inert (closed) the new object is inert too.

interface.name: newm_river_window_render_v1
interface.description: Scale and opacity of one window (both start at 1), and since version 2 its corner radius (starts at 0) and shadow (starts absent). Destroying the object returns all of them to their defaults with the next render_finish. Once the window's river_window_v1 is destroyed every request but destroy and snapshot is ignored.

entry.name: invalid_scale
entry.summary: scale is not greater than zero

request.name: destroy
request.description: The window returns to scale 1 and opacity 1 with the next render_finish.

request.name: set_scale
request.description:
Draw the whole window scaled by the given factor about the top-left corner of its river_node_v1 position: the window's surfaces, subsurfaces, popups, borders and decoration surfaces. The application is not resized and receives no new configure.
While the applied scale is not 1 the window receives no pointer, touch or tablet input: river still reports window_interaction and pointer_enter for it to the window manager, so a click picks the window, but the application sees no pointer focus. Keyboard focus is unaffected.
The scale must be greater than zero. This is rendering state, applied with the next render_finish. The default is 1.

request.name: set_opacity
request.description:
Multiply the alpha of every buffer and border of the window (popups included) by the given opacity, on top of any alpha-modifier-v1 multiplier the application sets.
The opacity must be within [0, 1]. This is rendering state, applied with the next render_finish. The default is 1.

request.name: set_corner_radius
request.description:
Round the corners of the window's content box (its dimensions at its river_node_v1 position) with the given radius in logical pixels. Every surface buffer of the window (decoration surfaces included) whose corner lies on a corner of that box is clipped to the rounded corner; buffers that do not reach a corner of the box, and popups, are not clipped. While borders are set on all four edges and the window is not clipped by set_clip_box or set_content_clip_box across them, the border is drawn as one outline around the rounded box, its outer radius the radius plus the border width.
The radius is scaled with set_scale. A fullscreen window is drawn with square corners and without shadow.
This is rendering state, applied with the next render_finish. The default is 0: square corners.

request.name: set_shadow

description.summary: draw a shadow below the window

request.description:
Draw a soft shadow below the window's surfaces, borders and decoration surfaces, but not inside the window's (rounded) content box. The box casting the shadow is the window's content box grown by spread on every side (its corner radius grown by spread too) and moved by offset_x, offset_y; the shadow fades out over softness logical pixels past that box (a Gaussian with a standard deviation of softness / 2).
The colour uses the 32-bit RGBA convention of river_window_v1.set_borders (premultiplied alpha) and is multiplied by set_opacity; the shadow is scaled with set_scale. It is not clipped by set_clip_box.
This is rendering state, applied with the next render_finish. The default is no shadow.

request.name: clear_shadow
request.description: Remove the shadow. This is rendering state, applied with the next render_finish.

request.name: snapshot

description.summary: keep a copy of the window's current frame

request.description:
Copy the window as river draws it now into a new scene node that river keeps drawing after the window is gone: its surface and decoration surface buffers, borders and shadow, with their current scale, opacity and corners. Popups are not copied. The copy sits directly above the window in the stacking order; when the window manager restacks windows river raises every snapshot above them. It takes no input.
For a close animation, make this request when river_window_v1.closed arrives, before destroying the river_window_v1: river still draws the window's last buffers until the render sequence that follows, and the copy takes over from it without a visible change.
Lifetime: the copy is drawn from this request until the first of (1) the client destroys the newm_river_snapshot_v1, (2) the client disconnects, (3) lifetime milliseconds pass (values are clamped to [1, 10000]): river then removes it and sends newm_river_snapshot_v1.expired. If the window is already destroyed, the object is created expired and expired is sent at once.

interface.name: newm_river_snapshot_v1

description.summary: a copy of a window's last frame

interface.description: Made by newm_river_window_render_v1.snapshot. Its origin is the window's river_node_v1 position at the time of the copy. set_position, set_scale and set_opacity are rendering state: they may only be made during a manage or render sequence and are applied with the next render_finish. After expired every request but destroy is ignored.

entry.name: invalid_scale
entry.summary: scale is not greater than zero

request.name: destroy
request.description: Remove the copy at once, not at the next render_finish.

request.name: set_position
request.description: Draw the copy's origin at x, y, in the coordinate space of river_node_v1.set_position. The default is where the window was.

request.name: set_scale
request.description: Draw the copy scaled about its origin by the given factor, relative to the size it was copied at (which already includes the window's own set_scale). It must be greater than zero. The default is 1.

request.name: set_opacity
request.description: Multiply the alpha of everything in the copy by the given opacity, within [0, 1]. The default is 1.

event.name: expired
event.description: The lifetime given to the snapshot request passed, or the window was already gone, and river removed the copy. The client should destroy the object.
